title: Staged observability upgrade with lightweight span router and compat shim
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Our current observability stack shows excessive exporter fanout and allocation hotspots during high-concurrency inference (especially under batching). Several customer incidents exposed increased tail latency correlated with trace forwarding spikes. We need a low-risk, staged approach to upgrade OpenTelemetry dependencies and introduce a lightweight span-router and compatibility shim so we can reduce runtime overhead without breaking legacy instrumentation.

Goals:
- Upgrade OTEL libraries to the latest approved patch (compatible with our runtime-ABI) in a staged fashion.
- Introduce a lightweight span-router that collapses duplicate/semantically-identical spans before export to reduce fanout to downstream exporters.
- Add a compat-shim for legacy log/trace emitters that performs structured conversion at the source (avoid on-path allocations later).
- Maintain backwards compatibility for existing collectors and retain trace fidelity for debugging.
- Roll out gradually with canaries and automated rollback criteria to protect SLOs.

Non-goals: full rewrite of exporter ecosystem, changing tracing semantics for customer-visible traces, or replacing existing backend exporters now.
acceptance_criteria: OTEL library upgraded on 10% canary runtime with no observable increase in p99 request latency or error rate for 48h
Span-router reduces exporter fanout (number of outgoing spans per request) by at least 25% in internal bench for mixed chat/generation workload
End-to-end memory allocations from tracing hotpath reduced by at least 18% in perf harness
Compat-shim converts legacy logs to structured form with <2ms added wall time on average and <0.5% CPU overhead increase at canary scale
Automated rollback triggers if p99 latency increases >7% or error rate increases >0.5% during rollout
tasks: Design span-router algorithm and invariants (collapsing rules, idempotency, non-lossy tagging)
Implement OTEL dependency bump with compatibility layer and feature flags
Build compat-shim for legacy logging emitters (Java/Go shim prototypes)
Integrate span-router into exporter pipeline with opt-in config per deployment
Add canary rollout orchestration (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and health checks
Run perf harness across representative workloads and record baselines
Documentation: migration notes, troubleshooting, and runbook for rollback
Postmortem / learnings doc and follow-up tickets for exporter-specific tweaks
comments: 2026-02-26 - Priya Nair: Initial spike showed a simple span collapse rule (same name + identical meta keys) reduces downstream events by ~33% on a synthetic batching workload.
2026-03-02 - Liam OConnor: Implemented proof-of-concept span-router in local fork. Prototype uses a fixed-size LRU to deduplicate recent spans; observed ~20% CPU decrease on node-level benchmarks.

2026-03-05 - Design review (Ava Rodriguez): Confirmed that collapsing should preserve a representative span with aggregated metadata; asked to include a trace-level flag to disable collapsing for debug runs.
2026-03-08 - Security (Noah Kim): Reviewed compat-shim; flagged that the shim must not ship encryption keys or secrets to logs. Confirmed design is safe with KMS-backed key usage left untouched.

2026-03-11 - Perf team (Marta Lopez): End-to-end harness run: allocations down 19% p50, exporter count per request down 28% on average, p95 latency unchanged. We should still run a longer 48h canary before broad rollout.
2026-03-13 - Liam OConnor: Added automated rollback hooks: if p99 latency > 7% over baseline or error-rate delta >0.5% we rollback to previous runtime-config. Canary orchestration drafted in runbook.
2026-03-14 - Priya Nair: RFC merged to trunk behind feature flag 'enable_span_router'. Next step: deploy 5% canary in staging region and monitor for 72 hours.
